name: Local vs Global Addressing in SVDAG
definition: Two addressing schemes for node pointers. Global addressing uses a single address space for the entire data structure. Local addressing uses separate address spaces for each node layer, where pointers are offsets from the start of that specific layer.
summary: Local vs Global Addressing in SVDAG defines two pointer schemes: global addressing uses a single address space for the entire graph, while local addressing uses per-layer offsets, enabling larger structures by limiting address space per layer rather than the total.
